gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on September 4?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 4 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent official forecasts from sources including the German Weather Service and global models indicate mostly clear skies and light westerly winds over Munich on September 4, supporting daytime maximum temperatures in the upper 20s °C under stable high-pressure conditions. These conditions favor strong solar heating with minimal cloud interference or precipitation, aligning with the market’s strong implied probability for a 29–30 °C high. Historical September 4 records show a 30.9 °C peak, while recent years have reached 28–29 °C, providing context for trader positioning. Updated model consensus and the absence of cooling fronts in the latest runs reinforce expectations near these thresholds ahead of final observations.

These conditions align with seasonal averages around 21°C while suppressing any spike above 23°C, explaining the market's heavy weighting toward 22°C at 52.5% implied probability. Westerly winds advect milder Atlantic air, and recent model runs have converged on modest afternoon peaks without significant clearing. Traders monitor updated Met Office observations and any late-day breaks in cloud cover that could nudge readings toward 23°C, though current guidance keeps higher outcomes below 5% odds.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 4 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Current forecast consensus from Met Office, GFS, and other models indicates a peak temperature of 21–22°C in London on September 4, 2026, driven by persistent cloud cover, light rain or drizzle in the morning, and moderate westerly winds that limit daytime heating.** 

These conditions follow a mild start to the month with typical early-autumn Atlantic airflow suppressing any strong warming. Afternoon clearing may allow brief rises toward 22–23°C in some areas, but overall model agreement keeps extremes unlikely. This scientific outlook—rooted in observed pressure patterns around 1013–1016 hPa and dew points supporting modest humidity—explains why traders have concentrated implied probability on the 21–23°C outcomes, with 22°C leading at 54%. Minor forecast revisions from new model runs could still shift the exact maximum before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Persistent rain and extensive cloud cover from a northeast-flowing system are capping daytime heating in Tokyo, keeping forecast highs clustered in the mid-20s Celsius for September 5.** Official guidance from the Japan Meteorological Agency and global models (including GFS and ECMWF runs) indicate overcast skies with light to moderate precipitation and northeasterly winds of 7–12 mph, which limit solar insolation and promote evaporative cooling. This setup produces a tight distribution around 25–26°C peaks, with hourly profiles showing afternoon maxima rarely exceeding 27°C amid high humidity (70–90%) and stable pressure near 1013–1014 hPa. Minor model differences in exact cloud timing and wind strength create the near-even split between 25°C and 26°C implied probabilities, while historical September averages near 29°C highlight how this transient pattern deviates from climatology. Fresh model updates overnight and morning observations will refine the final peak.

Surface high pressure and northerly advection of drier air are suppressing widespread cloud cover and allowing strong solar heating, yet the modest humidity and light flow keep the peak from climbing higher. The tight 40.5 %–37.5 % split between the 84–85 °F and 86–87 °F bins reflects lingering uncertainty in the precise timing of any clearing versus scattered cumulus that could shave a degree or two off the maximum. Historical climatology places the September 4 average at 80 °F, so current conditions remain modestly above normal but well below record territory.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest Japan Meteorological Agency guidance and ensemble forecasts point to a high of 25–26 °C in Tokyo on September 5 under persistent cloud cover and scattered rain. Northeasterly flow advects cooler, moist marine air while extensive stratiform clouds sharply reduce surface insolation, limiting afternoon warming. This pattern follows several days of similar conditions that have already depressed daytime maxima several degrees below September climatology. Model spread remains modest, with most runs clustering between 24–27 °C; the precise peak hinges on any brief afternoon clearing and exact rainfall timing. Traders therefore assign nearly equal weight to the two leading bins, reflecting the narrow but genuine forecast uncertainty around these thresholds.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 4 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Trader consensus reflected in the market-implied odds places the strongest probability on 24°C, with secondary support for 23°C and 25°C, consistent with typical model spread and uncertainty in exact rainfall timing and intensity. Updated model runs and official briefings from agencies like DWD will provide the next key data points ahead of resolution.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Trader consensus reflected in the 45.5% implied probability for 24°C aligns with this guidance, with smaller probabilities assigned to 25°C and 23°C capturing remaining model spread and uncertainty in exact timing of cloud cover. Final resolution will depend on official observations from Munich stations, with no major forecast shifts reported in the past 24 hours.

gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on September 6?

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from multiple models, including Met Office, ECMWF-influenced sources, and high-resolution guidance, converge on a daytime high of 23–24°C for Munich on September 6 under clear to mostly clear skies and light northeasterly winds. This reflects a post-frontal high-pressure regime drawing cooler continental air after warmer conditions earlier in the week. The September 6 climatological average high stands at 21.2°C, so current guidance sits modestly above normal but without strong warm advection or subsidence that would support 25°C or higher. Model consensus has remained stable in the latest runs, with minimal spread and low precipitation risk, supporting the market’s heavy weighting toward 23–24°C outcomes as the most probable range.

Seasonal normals for early September exceed 28°C, but current atmospheric conditions—enhanced moisture and reduced insolation—favor cooler outcomes. Ensemble guidance shows limited model spread, with minimal upside potential unless steering patterns shift. Updated model runs and JMA briefings through September 5 will refine resolution criteria for this discrete daily maximum.
